newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel shares close broadly higher.
newsitem.headline: Israel shares close broadly higher.

text.p: Israeli shares closed broadly higher on Monday with traders divided on the reasons for the rebound after a five-session losing streak.

"The fact that the Israelis and Palestinians are talking again was the main reason for today's rise. Despite the fact that it will be difficult to reach an agreement both sides know it is in their interests to continue peace talks," said Eyal Kolka at Sigma Securities.
But other traders said the political situation had no impact on the Tel Aviv stock exchange.
"The market recovered today but it's only a technical rebound. We saw five days of straight losses and prices regained lost ground," said Julien Assous at Sahar Securities.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 1.73 percent, or 4.22 points, to 247.80 on low all-share turnover of 84 million shekels against 70 million shekels on Sunday. The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.74 percent higher at 254.66.

"The market fell last week because of the political uncertainty concerning the peace process. The visit of King Hussein (on Sunday) helped to defuse tension and it seems now that negotiations with the Palestinians will resume soon," Kolka said.
"Volume continues to be extremely low indicating that investors are still waiting for further developments in the economy and politics," Assous said.
Israeli-PLO tensions have been high over Israel's decision to build 6,500 more homes for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem.

But Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu spoke by telephone with Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat on Sunday while Jordan's king was in Israel to visit the families of seven Israeli schoolchildren killed by a Jordanian soldier last Thursday.
Israeli and Palestinian officials met in Tel Aviv on Monday and Israel said it would allow Arafat to use the still unopened airport in the Gaza Strip for his personal flights.
However, violence could still flare over Netanyahu's pledge to break ground this week for the housing project at Jabal Abu Ghneim, called Har Homa by Israel, between East Jerusalem and Bethlehem.

Leumi Insurance Holdings fell 1.25 percent to 256 agorot. Bank Hapoalim said on Monday that Leumi Insurance is overpriced even though Assicurazioni Generali SPA of Italy is due to make a tender offer for the shares this week at a 28 percent premium.
The most active share was Bank Leumi which rose 1.5 percent to 536 agorot on turnover of 5.5 million shakels.
Koor Industries, the second active issue, climbed 1.75 percent to 30,878 agorot on volume of 4.7 million shekels.
Financial sources said Germany's Mannesmann AG is in negotiations with Koor to become a strategic partner in the company's United Steel Mills unit.
Teva Pharmaceutical Industries rose 1.0 percent to 20,065 agorot on volume of 3.8 million shekels.
